By multilinearity, readings with any converging finite list of coefficient vectors have the same limiting readings as their limits. Also (WS2) applies to the finitely many successor-degree basis words in (WS7). It bounds δk times every needed gradient by a quantity tending to zero on a slightly larger separated window. Interpolate from nearby sampled points to arbitrary separated points along short coordinate segments in that larger window. Their total length is O(δk). The fundamental theorem of calculus and (WS7) make the error tend to zero. The argument does not require a positive gap between distinct coordinate projections: the points themselves stay separated.
